The Drivers

Twelve themes, one pattern: millennial memory is always about place, loss, intimacy, the web, identity, expression, the future, care, witness, surveillance, emergence, and threshold.

● Place ● Loss ● Intimacy ● Web ● Identity ● Expression ● Future ● Care ● Witness ● Surveillance ● Emergence ● Threshold

Place

Places remembered, lost, transformed, or carried forward through memory.

"You can't google my hood."

Angela Mendoza

Place Loss

"I think the last remnants of real San Diego reside at the trolley stations."

Jack Hinzo

Place Intimacy

"Third Ave Chula Vista. I have memories attached to every inch of that street, north and south."

Alana Rodriguez

Place Identity

Loss

Things that disappeared: buildings, people, routines, neighborhoods, versions of self.

"How do you phantom limb a street?"

Jon Tobias

Loss Place

"I once came across one of my father's many notebooks and found a journal entry about me. I was a baby, and he described watching me sleep ... [It was] the first proof I had of his heart. I was 12 and I taped it on the back of my door. I've never been able to find it again."

Angela Mendoza

Loss Intimacy

"Not this is how I find out Horton Plaza doesn't exist anymore. Next you're gonna say Seaport Village isn't a thing anymore either."

a.benét

Loss Place

Web

Experiences mediated, preserved, distorted, or erased by digital life.

"If I type my current address into google and then street image the map, I can see Carol parked on the street in front of my apartment. There's probably a poem in there somewhere. Something about memory and google maps."

Jon Tobias

Web Place Loss

"I can't even find a picture of them on Google to prove they were real."

Alana Rodriguez

Web Loss

"I've always been a lay archivist and enjoyer of cultural artifacts."

Sam Yaziji

Web Identity

Intimacy

Friendship, family, vulnerability, and the private spaces where identity forms.

"I stepped on Zac Efron and Vanessa Hudgens every day until their faces became indiscernible. I loved those shoes so much."

Alana Rodriguez

Intimacy Identity

"I never want a reader to feel like they know me because they read my poems. You may know some of my story, but I'd like to think there's more to me than words."

a.benét

Intimacy Identity

"If you're vulnerable and practice it with care, there is always going to be someone who can relate. It gives people a chance to be seen."

Jon Tobias

Intimacy

Identity

Race, gender, culture, faith, and the ongoing work of becoming oneself.

"St. Porphyrios says, 'whoever wants to become a Christian must first become a poet.' "

Sam Yaziji

Identity Expression

"I grew up to love ghetto."

Angela Mendoza

Identity Place

"Boundaries don't exist ... "

a.benét

Identity

Expression

Art, poetry, music, and the drive to make meaning from experience.

"I thought poetry was what you went to when you wanted to talk about what you thought god was."

Jon Tobias

Expression Identity

"I begin a poem in a moment of anger or sorrow, and by writing the poem, I try to create something beautiful out of my abjection."

Sam Yaziji

Expression Intimacy

"I love anything that has to do with creation — crocheting, scrapbooking, photography, coloring. I was very proud of what new things I was able to make out of the old."

a.benét

Expression

Future

What comes next: transition, technology, hope, and the unknown.

"To the Roseland of the future: We'll always remember you the way you truly were."

Angela Mendoza

Future Place

"San Diego of the future, my hope is that you still hold space for community, that you don't close yourself off. I want third spaces and gardens. I want more BIPOC owned businesses, small and thriving."

a.benét

Future Place

"The older I get the more I want to crawl out of my city, into other parts of the world. I'm not really sure where I'm gonna end up."

Jack Hinzo

Future

Care

How we supported one another through everything the epoch demanded.

Witness

Who saw it, recorded it, and remembered it.

Surveillance

Who was watching, and what did visibility cost.

Emergence

What new forms of life, culture, and technology were taking shape.

Threshold

What worlds we were standing between.
